  intro C _ _ _ _ P _ hP _ X

  -- This construction only needs the separator clause of Definition 8.1.
  let copower (I : Type w) := sigmaObj (fun _ : I => P)

    Sigma.desc ((equivShrink (P ⟶ Y)).symm : Shrink.{w} (P ⟶ Y) → (P ⟶ Y))
  have evaluation_epi (Y : C) : Epi (evaluation Y) := by
    constructor
    intro Z f g hfg
    apply hP.def f g
    intro a
    have h := congrArg (fun z =>
      Sigma.ι (fun _ : Shrink.{w} (P ⟶ Y) => P) (equivShrink (P ⟶ Y) a) ≫ z) hfg
    simpa [evaluation, ← Category.assoc] using h
  let q := evaluation X
  have : Epi q := evaluation_epi X
  let t := evaluation (kernel q)
  have : Epi t := evaluation_epi (kernel q)
  let k := kernel.ι q
  -- Alphabeta Math's proof of normality in abelian categories, step 3.1, gives the cokernel
  -- property by dualizing step 2.1 in the opposite abelian category.
  -- The supplier's epi clause uses Abelian.epiIsCokernelOfKernel.
  -- Its hypotheses are the evaluation epi and the chosen limit kernel fork.
  obtain ⟨hq⟩ :=
    (NormalMorphismsInAbelianCategories C q).2.1
      (KernelFork.ofι k (kernel.condition q)) (kernelIsKernel q)

  -- of t. Transport the cokernel witness with its projection q fixed.
  have annihilates_iff ⦃Y : C⦄ (g : copower (Shrink.{w} (P ⟶ X)) ⟶ Y) :
      k ≫ g = 0 ↔ (t ≫ k) ≫ g = 0 := by
    rw [Category.assoc]
    constructor

by
  intros C _ _ J K _ _ X Y BX BY
  let : Fintype J := Fintype.ofFinite J
  let : Fintype K := Fintype.ofFinite K
  dsimp only
  intro hX hY
  -- Proposition 3.7 and Alphabeta Math's matrix correspondence step 2.2
  -- reconstruct a morphism by expanding the two identity sums. Definition 3.4
  -- supplies these sums as hX and hY on the actual bicones. The planned
  -- FiniteBiproductUniversalProperties converts these into bilimit witnesses
  -- or derives totality for bicones of chosen limits or colimits.
  -- Mathlib's biproduct.total concerns the selected HasBiproduct bicone.
  -- Here the reviewed hypotheses give the identities for BX and BY directly.
  have reconstruct (f : BX.pt ⟶ BY.pt) :
      f = ∑ k, ∑ j, BX.π j ≫ (BX.ι j ≫ f ≫ BY.π k) ≫ BY.ι k := by
    calc
      f = 𝟙 BX.pt ≫ f ≫ 𝟙 BY.pt := by simp
      _ = _ := by
        rw [← hX, ← hY]
        simp only [Preadditive.comp_sum, Preadditive.sum_comp, Category.assoc]
  refine ⟨?_, reconstruct, ?_, ?_⟩

    -- entries give equal summands for both finite indices.
    intro f f' h
    calc
      f = _ := reconstruct f
      _ = f' := by
        rw [reconstruct f']
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun k _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => ?_))
        exact congrArg (fun e : X j ⟶ Y k => BX.π j ≫ e ≫ BY.ι k)

    -- and use the middle orthogonality equations. Proposition 3.7 inserts
    -- hY directly into the fixed (l,j) entry and distributes. The target
    -- contributes its projection, and the finite sum ranges over K.
    intro L _ Z BZ _hZ f g l j
    have compose (a : X j ⟶ BY.pt) (b : BY.pt ⟶ Z l) :
        a ≫ b = ∑ k, (a ≫ BY.π k) ≫ BY.ι k ≫ b := by
      calc
        a ≫ b = a ≫ 𝟙 BY.pt ≫ b := by simp
        _ = _ := by
          simp only [← hY, Preadditive.sum_comp, Preadditive.comp_sum, Category.assoc]

    intro f f' k j
    simp only [Preadditive.add_comp, Preadditive.comp_add]

  intro R _

    -- of this direct sum. To identify the specified comparison, the article's
    -- finite-support argument checks evaluation on the inclusion generators.

-- The counit acts as the identity, and its linearity supplies agreement of
-- the recovered scalar action at every group-algebra element. The additive
-- group is unchanged, so equality of module structures suffices.
private theorem representationModule_roundTripModule (M : ModuleCat.{w} A) :
    (H ⋙ F).obj M = M := by
  have sameScalar := (Rep.counitIso (k := k) (G := G) (M := M)).hom.hom.map_smul

    intro a x

-- Transport along equality of those instances before using extensionality.
private theorem representationModule_repOf_eq {X : Type w} [AddCommGroup X]
    (P Q : Module k X)
    (ρ : @Representation k G X _ _ _ P) (σ : @Representation k G X _ _ _ Q)
    (sameModule : P = Q)
    (sameAction : ∀ (g : G) (x : X), (ρ g).toFun x = (σ g).toFun x) :
    @Rep.of k G _ _ X _ P ρ = @Rep.of k G _ _ X _ Q σ := by
  subst Q
  have h : ρ = σ := by
    ext g x
    exact sameAction g x
  rw [h]

-- Restriction along the scalar map recovers the original k-action. The
-- recovered action of each g is the action of [g], hence the original ρ g.
private theorem representationModule_roundTripRep (X : Rep.{w} k G) :
    (F ⋙ H).obj X = X := by
  have sameScalar := Representation.asModuleEquiv_symm_map_smul (k := k) (G := G) X.ρ
  have recoveredAction := Representation.ofModule_asModule_act (k := k) (G := G) X.ρ
  let recovered : Module k X := ((F ⋙ H).obj X).hV2
  let action : @Representation k G X _ _ _ recovered := ((F ⋙ H).obj X).ρ
  have sameModule : recovered = X.hV2 :=
    Module.ext' recovered X.hV2 fun a x => (sameScalar a x).symm
  have sameAction (g : G) (x : X) : (action g).toFun x = (X.ρ g).toFun x :=
    recoveredAction g x
  exact representationModule_repOf_eq recovered X.hV2 action X.ρ sameModule sameAction

        exact hSmall I X

    -- Proposition 4.9 gives the categorical equivalence in an abelian
    -- category. The reviewed module suppliers use one carrier universe.
    -- Here the free modules and M have independent universes, so we
    -- carry out the quotient argument of Propositions 5.4–5.5 directly.
    constructor

      refine ⟨LinearMap.range_le_ker_iff.mp hexact.le, ?_⟩
      intro N _ _ g hg

        hexact.ge.trans (LinearMap.range_le_ker_iff.mpr hg)

      -- identifies that quotient with M and gives uniqueness on M.
      let e := q.quotKerEquivOfSurjective hsurj
      let h := ((LinearMap.ker q).liftQ g hk).comp e.symm.toLinearMap
      have hh : h.comp q = g := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro z
        change (LinearMap.ker q).liftQ g hk (e.symm (q z)) = g z
        rw [LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective_symm_apply]
        exact Submodule.liftQ_apply _ _ _
      refine ⟨h, hh, ?_⟩

      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro m
      obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := hsurj m
      exact DFunLike.congr_fun (hh'.trans hh.symm) z
    · rintro ⟨hzero, hfactor⟩
      -- The checked NotesProofs.cokernel_universal_exact tests the quotient
      -- by range d in a common universe. Lift this quotient into the target
      -- universe of hfactor so that the same test works for mixed carriers.
      have hker : LinearMap.ker q ≤ LinearMap.range d := by
        let S := LinearMap.range d
        let lift : ((I →₀ R) ⧸ S) ≃ₗ[R] ULift.{max v x y} ((I →₀ R) ⧸ S) :=
          ULift.moduleEquiv.symm
        let p := lift.toLinearMap.comp S.mkQ
        have hp : p.comp d = 0 := by
          change (lift.toLinearMap.comp S.mkQ).comp d = 0
          rw [LinearMap.comp_assoc, LinearMap.range_mkQ_comp, LinearMap.comp_zero]

        change q z = 0 at hz
        have hpz : p z = 0 := by
          rw [← DFunLike.congr_fun hh z, LinearMap.comp_apply, hz, map_zero]
        change z ∈ S
        rw [← Submodule.ker_mkQ S]
        exact lift.injective (hpz.trans (map_zero lift).symm)
      refine ⟨le_antisymm (LinearMap.range_le_ker_iff.mpr hzero) hker, ?_⟩
      -- The quotient of M by range q also lifts into the specified target
      -- universe. Its quotient map and the zero map both factor the zero
      -- map through q. Uniqueness forces the quotient map to vanish.
      let T := LinearMap.range q
      let lift : (M ⧸ T) ≃ₗ[R] ULift.{max u w x y} (M ⧸ T) :=
        ULift.moduleEquiv.symm
      let p := lift.toLinearMap.comp T.mkQ
      have hp : p.comp q = 0 := by
        change (lift.toLinearMap.comp T.mkQ).comp q = 0
        rw [LinearMap.comp_assoc, LinearMap.range_mkQ_comp, LinearMap.comp_zero]
      obtain ⟨h, _, huniq⟩ :=
        hfactor (ULift.{max u w x y} (M ⧸ T)) 0 (LinearMap.zero_comp d)
      have hpzero : p = 0 :=
        (huniq p hp).trans (huniq 0 (LinearMap.zero_comp q)).symm
      intro m
      have hm : m ∈ T := by
        rw [← Submodule.ker_mkQ T]
        apply lift.injective
        exact (DFunLike.congr_fun hpzero m).trans (map_zero lift).symm

by
  intro C D _ _ _ _ e
  dsimp only
  -- Alphabeta Math's exact-equivalence proof, step 1.1. The equivalence
  -- preserves all existing limits and colimits, so use the parallel-pair
  -- shapes for kernels and cokernels and every discrete shape for coproducts.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-an-equivalence-between-abelian-categories-is-exact
  let preservesLimits : PreservesLimitsOfSize.{0, 0} e.functor :=
    Adjunction.isEquivalencePreservesLimits e.functor
  let preservesColimits : PreservesColimitsOfSize.{0, 0} e.functor :=
    Adjunction.isEquivalence_preservesColimits e.functor
  have hLimits : ∀ {A B : C} (f : A ⟶ B),
      PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) e.functor ∧
        PreservesColimit (parallelPair f 0) e.functor :=
    fun _ => ⟨preservesLimits.preservesLimitsOfShape.preservesLimit,
      preservesColimits.preservesColimitsOfShape.preservesColimit⟩
  have hCoproducts : ∀ (I : Type w), PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) e.functor :=
    fun I => (Adjunction.isEquivalence_preservesColimits e.functor).preservesColimitsOfShape
  -- Step 2.1 uses the additive categories underlying the abelian categories.
  -- The compiled supplier takes zero-object and finite (co)product preservation.
  have hZero (X : C) (hX : IsZero X) : IsZero (e.functor.obj X) := by
    let : PreservesLimit (Functor.empty C) e.functor :=
      preservesLimits.preservesLimitsOfShape.preservesLimit

  let : PreservesFiniteLimits e.functor :=
    PreservesLimitsOfSize0.preservesFiniteLimits e.functor
  let : PreservesFiniteColimits e.functor :=
    PreservesColimitsOfSize0.preservesFiniteColimits e.functor

  let : HasFiniteBiproducts D := Abelian.hasFiniteBiproducts

    (AdditiveFunctorsAndBiproducts e.functor).2 hZero inferInstance inferInstance
  refine ⟨inferInstance, hLimits, hCoproducts, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- The reviewed endpoint uses exact short complexes. Finite limit and
    -- colimit preservation gives both homology preservation instances for Exact.map.
    intro _ S hS
    exact hS.map e.functor
  · -- The progenerator corollary, steps 2.4 and 3.1, transports existence for
    -- the discrete shapes required here. Steps 2.1 and 2.3 give the two object
    -- properties through the projective-object and separator suppliers.
    intro hC
    let hD : HasCoproducts.{w} D :=
      fun I => Adjunction.hasColimitsOfShape_of_equivalence (J := Discrete I) e.inverse
    refine ⟨hD, ?_⟩

    refine ⟨Functor.PreservesProjectiveObjects.projective_obj (F := e.functor) hProjective,
      hSeparator.of_equivalence e, ?_⟩

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits
private theorem abelianEquivalenceSmallness
    {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₂} D]
    [Preadditive C] [Preadditive D] (e : C ≌ D) [e.functor.Additive]
    {I : Type w} [DecidableEq I] [HasCoproducts.{w} C] [HasCoproducts.{w} D]
    (P : C) (Y : I → D)
    (h : Function.Bijective
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid (β := fun i => P ⟶ e.inverse.obj (Y i))
        (fun i => Preadditive.rightComp P (Sigma.ι (fun j => e.inverse.obj (Y j)) i)))) :
    Function.Bijective
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid (β := fun i => e.functor.obj P ⟶ Y i)
        (fun i => Preadditive.rightComp (e.functor.obj P) (Sigma.ι Y i))) := by
  -- Alphabeta Math's progenerator corollary, steps 1.1 and 2.2, uses the
  -- adjoint-equivalence transposition and coproduct preservation by the inverse.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-equivalences-preserve-progenerators
  let : PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) e.inverse :=
    (Adjunction.isEquivalence_preservesColimits e.inverse).preservesColimitsOfShape
  let X := fun i => e.inverse.obj (Y i)
  let compareC := DirectSum.toAddMonoid (β := fun i => P ⟶ X i)
    (fun i => Preadditive.rightComp P (Sigma.ι X i))
  let compareD := DirectSum.toAddMonoid (β := fun i => e.functor.obj P ⟶ Y i)
    (fun i => Preadditive.rightComp (e.functor.obj P) (Sigma.ι Y i))
  let mapSummand := fun i => e.toAdjunction.homAddEquiv P (Y i)
  let mapSum : DirectSum I (fun i => e.functor.obj P ⟶ Y i) ≃+
      DirectSum I (fun i => P ⟶ X i) :=
    DFinsupp.mapRange.addEquiv mapSummand
  let coproductIso := (asIso (sigmaComparison e.inverse Y)).symm
  let postcompose : (P ⟶ e.inverse.obj (∐ Y)) ≃+ (P ⟶ ∐ X) :=
    { coproductIso.homToEquiv with
      map_add' := fun f g => Preadditive.add_comp _ _ _ f g coproductIso.hom }
  let mapCoproduct := (e.toAdjunction.homAddEquiv P (∐ Y)).trans postcompose

  -- Identify the actual comparison in Lemma 10.3 by checking the inclusions.
  have hSquare : mapCoproduct.toAddMonoidHom.comp compareD =
      compareC.comp mapSum.toAddMonoidHom := by
    apply DirectSum.addHom_ext
    intro i f
    have hSummand :
        mapSum (DirectSum.of (fun j => e.functor.obj P ⟶ Y j) i f) =
          DirectSum.of (fun j => P ⟶ X j) i (mapSummand i f) := by
      change DFinsupp.mapRange.addEquiv mapSummand (DFinsupp.single i f) =
        DFinsupp.single i (mapSummand i f)
      rw [DFinsupp.mapRange.addEquiv_apply, DFinsupp.mapRange_single]
    change mapCoproduct (compareD (DirectSum.of (fun j => e.functor.obj P ⟶ Y j) i f)) =
      compareC (mapSum (DirectSum.of (fun j => e.functor.obj P ⟶ Y j) i f))
    simp only [hSummand, compareC, compareD, DirectSum.toAddMonoid_of]
    change e.toAdjunction.homEquiv P (∐ Y) (f ≫ Sigma.ι Y i) ≫ coproductIso.hom =
      e.toAdjunction.homEquiv P (Y i) f ≫ Sigma.ι X i
    rw [e.toAdjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right, Category.assoc]
    congr 1
    exact map_ι_comp_inv_sigmaComparison e.inverse Y i
  apply (mapCoproduct.bijective.of_comp_iff' compareD).mp
  change Function.Bijective (⇑(mapCoproduct.toAddMonoidHom.comp compareD))
  rw [hSquare]
  exact h.comp mapSum.bijective

BalancedTensorUniversalProperty.proof:
by
  intro R _ B _ _ M _ _ Bal Universal
  -- Alphabeta Math, steps 1.1–6.1:
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products
  -- Step 1.1 works directly with additive homomorphisms. The right action
  -- from Definition 6.1 is the given opposite-ring module action.
  -- For steps 2.1–4.1 we use the coordinator's checked ChoiceFreeWatts
  -- quotient of a free additive group (NotesProofs/WattsSupport.lean,
  -- SHA-256 853d1dd0016bf0735f7a84559e2f1cbbb701fc3cb0e00395a0e138ffecb1f967).
  -- Its relation includes commutativity
  -- as well as the two additivity laws and balance. The planned free-module
  -- and linear-quotient theorems describe the notes' integer-module model.
  -- The separate Finsupp model in ModuleTensorUniversalProperty would need a
  -- pure-preserving comparison. Mathlib's TensorProduct.liftAddHom requires
  -- a commutative base semiring; the quotient here works for the given Ring R.
  -- ULift puts the carrier in the common universe of the reviewed statement.
  let right : R → B → B := fun r b => MulOpposite.op r • b
  let V := ChoiceFreeWatts.Tensor right M
  let inst : AddCommGroup V := ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorAddCommGroup right
  let T := AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{t} V)
  let lift : V ≃+ T := AddEquiv.ulift.symm
  let pure : Bal T :=
    ⟨fun b m => lift (ChoiceFreeWatts.pure right b m),
     fun b b' m => (congrArg lift ((ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced (X := M) right).1 b b' m)).trans
       (map_add lift _ _),
     fun b m m' => (congrArg lift ((ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced (X := M) right).2.1 b m m')).trans
       (map_add lift _ _),
     fun r b m => congrArg lift ((ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced (X := M) right).2.2 r b m)⟩
  have universal : Universal T pure := by
    intro A
    -- Step 1.2: restricting an additive map preserves all three laws.
    let restrict (h : AddMonoidHom T A) : Bal A :=
      ⟨fun b m => h (pure.val b m),
       fun b b' m => (congrArg h (pure.property.1 b b' m)).trans (map_add h _ _),
       fun b m m' => (congrArg h (pure.property.2.1 b m m')).trans (map_add h _ _),
       fun r b m => congrArg h (pure.property.2.2 r b m)⟩
    -- Steps 2.1–4.1: tensorLift extends the map on pairs and descends
    -- through the relations. Its input is exactly f.property, and
    -- commutativity in A takes care of the commutation relations.
    let extend (f : Bal A) : AddMonoidHom T A :=
      (ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLift right f.val f.property).comp lift.symm.toAddMonoidHom
    have extend_pure (f : Bal A) (b : B) (m : M) :
        extend f (pure.val b m) = f.val b m := by
      change (ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLift right f.val f.property)
        (lift.symm (lift (ChoiceFreeWatts.pure right b m))) = f.val b m
      rw [lift.symm_apply_apply]
      exact ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLift_pure right f.val f.property b m
    -- Step 5.1: the lift has the required values. The supplier's
    -- extensionality applies to the composites on the unlifted quotient.
    refine ⟨⟨restrict, extend, ?_, ?_⟩, fun _ _ _ => rfl⟩
    · intro h
      have hcomp := ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorExt right
        ((extend (restrict h)).comp lift.toAddMonoidHom) (h.comp lift.toAddMonoidHom)
        (extend_pure (restrict h))
      apply AddMonoidHom.ext
      intro x
      obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := lift.surjective x
      exact DFunLike.congr_fun hcomp z
    · intro f
      exact Subtype.ext (funext fun b => funext fun m => extend_pure f b m)
  -- Step 6.1: the relations apply to all pairs, including when a factor
  -- is zero or the ring is the zero ring.
  refine ⟨T, pure, universal, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x
    obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := lift.surjective x
    exact tensorFiniteSum lift.toAddMonoidHom z
  · -- Theorem 6.2 also asks for uniqueness of the representing group.
    -- Use both given precomposition equivalences to get maps in both
    -- directions. Their composites are identities by injectivity of
    -- precomposition, which also gives uniqueness of the isomorphism.
    intro T' pure' universal'
    have homExt (U A : AddCommGrpCat.{max v w t}) (p : Bal U)
        (rep : Universal U p) (f g : AddMonoidHom U A)
        (h : ∀ b m, f (p.val b m) = g (p.val b m)) : f = g := by
      obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := rep A
      exact e.injective (Subtype.ext (funext fun b => funext fun m =>
        (he f b m).trans ((h b m).trans (he g b m).symm)))
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := universal T'
    obtain ⟨e', he'⟩ := universal' T
    let f := e.symm pure'
    let g := e'.symm pure
    have hf (b : B) (m : M) : f (pure.val b m) = pure'.val b m := by
      rw [← he, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    have hg (b : B) (m : M) : g (pure'.val b m) = pure.val b m := by
      rw [← he', Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    have hgf : g.comp f = AddMonoidHom.id T := homExt T T pure universal _ _ fun b m => by
      rw [AddMonoidHom.comp_apply, hf, hg, AddMonoidHom.id_apply]
    have hfg : f.comp g = AddMonoidHom.id T' := homExt T' T' pure' universal' _ _ fun b m => by
      rw [AddMonoidHom.comp_apply, hg, hf, AddMonoidHom.id_apply]
    let iso : T ≃+ T' :=
      { f with
        invFun := g
        left_inv := DFunLike.congr_fun hgf
        right_inv := DFunLike.congr_fun hfg }
    refine ⟨iso, hf, ?_⟩
    intro j hj
    have h := homExt T T' pure universal j.toAddMonoidHom f (fun b m => (hj b m).trans (hf b m).symm)
    exact AddEquiv.ext (fun x => congrArg (fun k : AddMonoidHom T T' => k x) h)

section Witness

variable {R : Type u} [Ring R] {B : Type v} [AddCommGroup B] [Module (MulOpposite R) B]
  {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

local notation "right" => (fun (r : R) (b : B) => MulOpposite.op r • b)

local instance : AddCommGroup (ChoiceFreeWatts.Tensor right M) :=
  ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorAddCommGroup right

-- Ian X, Theorem 6.2, p. 18, https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf#page=18
-- The notes absorb integer coefficients in the first factor of a pure tensor.
-- In the coordinator's presentation, induction on a free additive word gives
-- signed generators instead. Absorb each minus sign using first-variable
-- additivity and cancellation, and combine the two lists for a sum of words.
private theorem tensorFiniteSum {D : Type a} [AddCommGroup D]
    (h : ChoiceFreeWatts.Tensor right M →+ D) (x : ChoiceFreeWatts.Tensor right M) :
    ∃ pairs : List (B × M), (pairs.map fun bm => h (ChoiceFreeWatts.pure right bm.1 bm.2)).sum = h x := by
  refine AddCon.induction_on x ?_
  intro z
  change ∃ pairs : List (B × M), _ = (h.comp (ChoiceFreeWatts.wordMk _)) z
  let q := h.comp (ChoiceFreeWatts.wordMk (ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorRel right M))
  refine FreeAddGroup.induction_on (motive := fun z =>
    ∃ pairs : List (B × M), (pairs.map fun bm => h (ChoiceFreeWatts.pure right bm.1 bm.2)).sum = q z) z ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · exact ⟨[], (map_zero q).symm⟩
  · intro bm
    exact ⟨[bm], by simp [q, ChoiceFreeWatts.pure, ChoiceFreeWatts.wordGen]⟩
  · rintro ⟨b, m⟩ _
    refine ⟨[(-b, m)], ?_⟩
    have hadd := (ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced (X := M) right).1
    have hzero : ChoiceFreeWatts.pure right (0 : B) m = 0 := by
      apply add_left_cancel (a := ChoiceFreeWatts.pure right (0 : B) m)
      simpa only [zero_add, add_zero] using (hadd 0 0 m).symm
    have hneg : ChoiceFreeWatts.pure right (-b) m = -ChoiceFreeWatts.pure right b m := by
      apply eq_neg_of_add_eq_zero_left
      rw [← hadd, neg_add_cancel, hzero]
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.sum_cons, List.sum_nil, add_zero, map_neg]
    rw [hneg, map_neg]
    rfl
  · intro x y hx hy
    obtain ⟨xs, hxs⟩ := hx
    obtain ⟨ys, hys⟩ := hy
    exact ⟨xs ++ ys, by rw [List.map_append, List.sum_append, hxs, hys, map_add]⟩

end Witness

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits in
by
  intro C _ _ _ _ P _ hGenerator hSmall

  let H := preadditiveCoyonedaObj P

  let leg (i : I) : H.obj P ⟶ H.obj (sigmaObj A) := H.map (Sigma.ι A i)
  -- Lemma 8.5 first identifies H(P) with the regular left R-module.
  -- The regular-module supplier concerns endomorphisms *in ModuleCat*.
  -- Here P is an arbitrary object, so use unop and check linearity for
  -- the actual precomposition action.
  let unopAdd : R ≃+ H.obj P := MulOpposite.opAddEquiv.symm.trans End.addEquiv
  let regular : R ≃ₗ[R] H.obj P :=
    { unopAdd with map_smul' := fun _ _ => rfl }
  -- Alphabeta Math's Hom functor step 2.1 uses smallness of P for
  -- the underlying additive map. The linear map below has that same
  -- underlying map because the legs act by postcomposition.
  -- Following the free-module steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1, assemble the
  -- maps on copies of R and evaluate them at coefficient one. The
  -- direct-sum equivalences implement the proposed Finsupp comparison
  -- without expanding a finite linear combination. Its source carrier
  -- can be larger than the target ModuleCat universe.
  let sumComparison : DirectSum I (fun _ => ↥(H.obj P)) →ₗ[R] H.obj (sigmaObj A) :=
    DirectSum.toModule R I (H.obj (sigmaObj A)) (fun i => (leg i).hom)
  have hSum : Function.Bijective sumComparison := hSmall I A
  let freeSum : (I →₀ R) ≃ₗ[R] DirectSum I (fun _ => ↥(H.obj P)) :=
    (finsuppLEquivDirectSum R R I).trans (DirectSum.congrLinearEquiv fun _ => regular)
  let θ : (I →₀ R) →ₗ[R] H.obj (sigmaObj A) := sumComparison.comp freeSum.toLinearMap
  have hθ : Function.Bijective θ := hSum.comp freeSum.bijective
  have hBasis (i : I) : θ (Finsupp.single i 1) = Sigma.ι A i := by
    change sumComparison (freeSum (Finsupp.single i 1)) = _
    simp only [freeSum, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, finsuppLEquivDirectSum_single,
      DirectSum.congrLinearEquiv_toLinearMap, ← LinearEquiv.coe_coe, DirectSum.lmap_lof,
      sumComparison, DirectSum.toModule_lof]
    change CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryStruct.id P) (Sigma.ι A i) = Sigma.ι A i
    exact Category.id_comp _
  -- Lift H(q) ≫ t on the individual generators. Alphabeta Math's
  -- free-module step 4.1 gives equality on the whole free module,
  -- via the first clause of the checked free-module supplier.
  let s : H.obj (sigmaObj A) ⟶ H.obj Y := CategoryStruct.comp (H.map q) t
  let images (i : I) : P ⟶ Y := s.hom (Sigma.ι A i)
  let g : sigmaObj A ⟶ Y := Sigma.desc images
  have hg : H.map g = s := by
    have hgBasis (i : I) : (H.map g).hom (θ (Finsupp.single i 1)) = images i := by
      rw [hBasis]
      exact Sigma.ι_comp_desc images i
    have hsBasis (i : I) : s.hom (θ (Finsupp.single i 1)) = images i := by
      rw [hBasis]
    obtain ⟨f, _, hf⟩ := (FreeModulesAndPresentations.{v, v, w, 0, 0} R (H.obj Y)).1 images
    have heq : (H.map g).hom.comp θ = s.hom.comp θ :=
      (hf _ hgBasis).trans (hf _ hsBasis).symm
    apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro z
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hθ.2 z
    exact DFunLike.congr_fun heq a
  have hdg : CategoryStruct.comp d g = 0 := by
    apply H.map_injective
    rw [H.map_comp, hg, H.map_zero]
    simp only [s, ← Category.assoc, ← H.map_comp, hdq, H.map_zero, zero_comp]
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' hq g hdg
  change CategoryStruct.comp q f = g at hf
  have hqf : CategoryStruct.comp (H.map q) (H.map f) = CategoryStruct.comp (H.map q) t := by
    rw [← H.map_comp, hf]
    exact hg
  -- Alphabeta Math's Hom functor steps 3.1 and 4.1 use cokernel
  -- preservation. Lemma 8.3 supplies it for the parallel pair (d, 0).
  -- The mapped cofork is a cokernel, so its projection is epic and
  -- therefore surjective in ModuleCat. The construction uses the
  -- lecture notes' ordinary choice for the chosen coproducts and
  -- cokernels, and Classical.decEq for finitely supported coordinates.
  let _ : PreservesColimit (parallelPair d 0) H := hExact.2.1 d
  have hMapQ := isColimitCoforkMapOfIsColimit' H hdq hq
  have hEpi : Epi (H.map q) := epi_of_isColimit_cofork hMapQ
  have hSurj := (ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective (H.map q)).mp hEpi
  refine ⟨f, ModuleCat.hom_ext (LinearMap.ext fun z => ?_)⟩
  obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hSurj z
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun (congrArg ModuleCat.Hom.hom hqf) a

external.usage: Implements H with the opposite endomorphism ring action by precomposition. Its linear map on each morphism is postcomposition, which identifies the image coproduct legs and the restriction of the lifted map.
Assembles the image coproduct legs into a linear map whose underlying additive map is the comparison in the smallness hypothesis. The evaluation lemma computes the comparison on each summand.
Identifies the free Finsupp module with the direct sum of copies of the ring and sends each singleton to the corresponding coordinate inclusion.
Takes the direct sum of the local linear equivalences from the regular left module to H(P), preserving the individual summand inclusions.
Uses the registered preservation clause at parallelPair d 0 and the supplied cokernel witness to identify H(q) as a cokernel projection of H(d).
Converts the epimorphism H(q) into surjectivity on module elements, allowing equality after precomposition with H(q) to determine the original linear map.

BimoduleTensorFunctoriality.support:
namespace BimoduleTensorFunctorialityAux

open CategoryTheory

universe r s v w t

variable {R : Type r} [Ring R] {S : Type s} [Ring S]

private abbrev Bimod (R : Type r) [Ring R] (S : Type s) [Ring S] :=
  AdditiveFunctor (SingleObj (MulOpposite R)) (ModuleCat.{v} S)

local notation "★" => SingleObj.star (MulOpposite R)

private abbrev carrier (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) := B.obj.obj ★

-- SingleObj composes f ≫ g as g * f. In the opposite ring this makes
-- the arrow for a * a' act by first applying a and then a'. Functoriality
-- gives the unit and product laws, and additivity gives the scalar sum law.
private abbrev action (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (a : R) (b : carrier B) : carrier B :=
  (B.obj.map (show ★ ⟶ ★ from MulOpposite.op a)) b

private theorem action_commutes (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (a : R) (c : S) (b : carrier B) :
    action B a (c • b) = c • action B a b :=
  map_smul (B.obj.map (show ★ ⟶ ★ from MulOpposite.op a)).hom c b

private theorem map_action {B B' : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S} (u : B ⟶ B') (a : R)
    (b : carrier B) :
    (u.hom.app ★) (action B a b) = action B' a ((u.hom.app ★) b) :=
  DFunLike.congr_fun (congrArg ModuleCat.Hom.hom
    (u.hom.naturality (show ★ ⟶ ★ from MulOpposite.op a))) b

-- Ian X, Proposition 6.3, p. 19.
-- https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf#page=19
-- Alphabeta Math, steps 1.2, 2.1, 3.1 and 5.1.
-- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products
-- Step 1.2 gives the left-handed pairing. The S-linearity of the right
-- action gives the commuting-action hypothesis, so outerModule implements
-- the left-handed descent of steps 2.1 and 3.1, and scale_pure evaluates it.
-- We use the concrete quotient of BalancedTensorUniversalProperty so the
-- same chosen tensor objects carry the actions and all the induced maps.
-- The checked supplier is NotesProofs/WattsSupport.lean, SHA-256
-- 853d1dd0016bf0735f7a84559e2f1cbbb701fc3cb0e00395a0e138ffecb1f967.
-- ULift supplies the additional carrier universe in the reviewed endpoint.
private abbrev Tensor (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :=
  ChoiceFreeWatts.Tensor (action B) M

local instance (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    AddCommGroup (Tensor B M) :=
  ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorAddCommGroup (action B)

local instance (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    Module S (Tensor B M) :=
  ChoiceFreeWatts.outerModule (action B) (action_commutes B)

private abbrev obj (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    ModuleCat.{max v w t} S :=
  ModuleCat.of S (ULift.{t} (Tensor B M))

private abbrev pure (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R)
    (b : carrier B) (m : M) : obj.{r,s,v,w,t} B M :=
  ULift.up (ChoiceFreeWatts.pure (action B) b m)

private theorem pure_balanced (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    ChoiceFreeWatts.Balanced (action B) (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M) := by
  have h := ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced (X := M) (action B)
  exact ⟨fun b b' m => congrArg ULift.up (h.1 b b' m),
    fun b m m' => congrArg ULift.up (h.2.1 b m m'),
    fun a b m => congrArg ULift.up (h.2.2 a b m)⟩

private theorem smul_pure (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R)
    (c : S) (b : carrier B) (m : M) :
    c • pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m = pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M (c • b) m :=
  congrArg ULift.up (ChoiceFreeWatts.scale_pure (action B) (action_commutes B) c b m)

-- Step 5.1 uses uniqueness on pure tensors. Transport tensorLift and
-- tensorLift_pure through the lift, and use tensorExt for uniqueness.
private theorem unique_lift (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R)
    (A : AddCommGrpCat.{max v w t}) (p : carrier B → M → A)
    (hp : ChoiceFreeWatts.Balanced (action B) p) :
    ∃! h : obj.{r,s,v,w,t} B M →+ A, ∀ b m, h (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m) = p b m := by
  let up : Tensor B M ≃+ ULift.{t} (Tensor B M) := AddEquiv.ulift.symm
  let h := ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLift (action B) p hp
  have eval (b : carrier B) (m : M) : h (ChoiceFreeWatts.pure (action B) b m) = p b m :=
    ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLift_pure (action B) p hp b m
  refine ⟨h.comp up.symm.toAddMonoidHom, eval, ?_⟩
  intro g hg
  have eq : g.comp up.toAddMonoidHom = h :=
    ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorExt (action B) _ _ (fun b m => (hg b m).trans (eval b m).symm)
  ext x
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun eq x.down

private theorem hom_ext {B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S} {M : ModuleCat.{w} R}
    {Y : ModuleCat.{max v w t} S} {f g : obj.{r,s,v,w,t} B M ⟶ Y}
    (h : ∀ b m, f (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m) = g (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m)) : f = g := by
  let up : Tensor B M ≃+ ULift.{t} (Tensor B M) := AddEquiv.ulift.symm
  have eq : f.hom.toAddMonoidHom.comp up.toAddMonoidHom =
      g.hom.toAddMonoidHom.comp up.toAddMonoidHom :=
    ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorExt (action B) _ _ h
  apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun eq x.down

-- Proposition 6.3 extends the portal's descent argument to morphisms.
-- Naturality supplies right equivariance of u. The linearity of f supplies
-- left equivariance on the second factor. Left equivariance of u then
-- supplies the outer-linearity hypothesis of tensorLinearLift.
private theorem map_balanced {B B' : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S} {M M' : ModuleCat.{w} R}
    (u : B ⟶ B') (f : M ⟶ M') :
    ChoiceFreeWatts.Balanced (action B)
      (fun b m => pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M' ((u.hom.app ★) b) (f m)) := by
  have hp := pure_balanced.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M'
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro b b' m
    simp only [map_add, hp.1]
  · intro b m m'
    simp only [map_add, hp.2.1]
  · intro a b m
    dsimp only
    rw [map_action, hp.2.2, map_smul]

private theorem map_outer_linear {B B' : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S} {M M' : ModuleCat.{w} R}
    (u : B ⟶ B') (f : M ⟶ M') (c : S) (b : carrier B) (m : M) :
    pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M' ((u.hom.app ★) (c • b)) (f m) =
      c • pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M' ((u.hom.app ★) b) (f m) := by
  rw [map_smul, smul_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}]

private def map {B B' : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S} {M M' : ModuleCat.{w} R}
    (u : B ⟶ B') (f : M ⟶ M') :
    obj.{r,s,v,w,t} B M ⟶ obj.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M' :=
  ModuleCat.ofHom <|
    (ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLinearLift (action B) (action_commutes B)
      (fun b m => pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M' ((u.hom.app ★) b) (f m))
      (map_balanced.{r,s,v,w,t} u f) (map_outer_linear.{r,s,v,w,t} u f)).comp
        ULift.moduleEquiv.toLinearMap

private theorem map_pure {B B' : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S} {M M' : ModuleCat.{w} R}
    (u : B ⟶ B') (f : M ⟶ M') (b : carrier B) (m : M) :
    map.{r,s,v,w,t} u f (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m) =
      pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M' ((u.hom.app ★) b) (f m) :=
  ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLinearLift_pure (action B) (action_commutes B)
    (fun b m => pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M' ((u.hom.app ★) b) (f m))
    (map_balanced.{r,s,v,w,t} u f) (map_outer_linear.{r,s,v,w,t} u f) b m

-- Use step 5.1's pure-tensor extensionality for identities, composition
-- and separate additivity. Fixing either factor keeps its identity map.
private def tensorFunctor :
    Bimod.{r,s,v} R S × ModuleCat.{w} R ⥤ ModuleCat.{max v w t} S where
  obj X := obj.{r,s,v,w,t} X.1 X.2
  map f := map.{r,s,v,w,t} f.1 f.2
  map_id X := by
    apply hom_ext
    intro b m
    change map.{r,s,v,w,t} (𝟙 X.1) (𝟙 X.2) (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} X.1 X.2 b m) =
      pure.{r,s,v,w,t} X.1 X.2 b m
    rw [map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}]
    rfl
  map_comp f g := by
    apply hom_ext
    intro b m
    change map.{r,s,v,w,t} (f.1 ≫ g.1) (f.2 ≫ g.2) (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} _ _ b m) =
      map.{r,s,v,w,t} g.1 g.2 (map.{r,s,v,w,t} f.1 f.2 (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} _ _ b m))
    rw [map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}, map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}, map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}]
    rfl

private theorem sectL_additive (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    ((Prod.sectL (Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) M) ⋙ tensorFunctor.{r,s,v,w,t}).Additive := by
  constructor
  intro B B' u u'
  change map.{r,s,v,w,t} (u + u') (𝟙 M) =
    map.{r,s,v,w,t} u (𝟙 M) + map.{r,s,v,w,t} u' (𝟙 M)
  apply hom_ext.{r,s,v,w,t}
  intro b m
  change map.{r,s,v,w,t} (u + u') (𝟙 M) (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m) =
    map.{r,s,v,w,t} u (𝟙 M) (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m) +
      map.{r,s,v,w,t} u' (𝟙 M) (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m)
  rw [map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}, map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}, map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}]
  exact (pure_balanced.{r,s,v,w,t} B' M).1 _ _ _

private theorem sectR_additive (B : Bimod.{r,s,v} R S) :
    ((Prod.sectR B (ModuleCat.{w} R)) ⋙ tensorFunctor.{r,s,v,w,t}).Additive := by
  constructor
  intro M M' f f'
  change map.{r,s,v,w,t} (𝟙 B) (f + f') =
    map.{r,s,v,w,t} (𝟙 B) f + map.{r,s,v,w,t} (𝟙 B) f'
  apply hom_ext.{r,s,v,w,t}
  intro b m
  change map.{r,s,v,w,t} (𝟙 B) (f + f') (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m) =
    map.{r,s,v,w,t} (𝟙 B) f (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m) +
      map.{r,s,v,w,t} (𝟙 B) f' (pure.{r,s,v,w,t} B M b m)
  rw [map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}, map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}, map_pure.{r,s,v,w,t}]
  exact (pure_balanced.{r,s,v,w,t} B M').2.1 _ _ _

end BimoduleTensorFunctorialityAux

external.usage: Precompose the outer-linear balanced lift with the S-linear ULift.down equivalence to obtain the tensor morphism in the reviewed carrier universe. Its action on ULift.up of a pure tensor reduces definitionally to the original pure tensor.

ReconstructionFromSmallProjectiveGenerat.proof:
(open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits in
by
  intro C _ _ _ _ P _ hGenerator hSmall
  dsimp only
  let R := (End P)ᵐᵒᵖ
  let H : Functor C (ModuleCat.{v} R) := preadditiveCoyonedaObj P
  change ∃ L : Functor (ModuleCat.{v} R) C,
    Nonempty (Iso (Functor.comp L H) (Functor.id (ModuleCat.{v} R))) ∧
    Nonempty (Iso (Functor.comp H L) (Functor.id C))
  have hHom : ∀ X Y, Function.Bijective (H.map (X := X) (Y := Y)) :=
    GeneratorHomFullyFaithful C P hGenerator hSmall
  let _ : H.Full := ⟨fun {X Y} => (hHom X Y).2⟩
  let _ : H.Faithful := ⟨fun {X Y} => (hHom X Y).1⟩
  have hExact := GeneratorHomExactnessAndDetection C P hGenerator hSmall

  -- Alphabeta Math, step 1.1. The portal starts with an adjunction and
  -- computes its unit on free modules. Here we construct the underlying
  -- free-term comparison, as in Lemma 8.5 of the lecture notes. Unop
  -- identifies the regular left module with H(P): multiplication in R
  -- becomes precomposition. The linear sum of mapped coproduct legs
  -- has the same underlying additive map as the smallness hypothesis.
  -- The coefficient-one vector in a summand therefore maps to its
  -- coproduct injection, and the comparison also covers the empty sum.
  have hFree (I : Type v) :
      Nonempty (ModuleCat.of R (I →₀ R) ≅ H.obj (sigmaObj (fun _ : I => P))) := by
    let _ : DecidableEq I := Classical.decEq I
    let A : I → C := fun _ => P
    let unopAdd : R ≃+ H.obj P := MulOpposite.opAddEquiv.symm.trans End.addEquiv
    let regular : R ≃ₗ[R] H.obj P :=
      { unopAdd with map_smul' := fun _ _ => rfl }
    let sumComparison : DirectSum I (fun _ => ↥(H.obj P)) →ₗ[R] H.obj (sigmaObj A) :=
      DirectSum.toModule R I (H.obj (sigmaObj A))
        (fun i => (H.map (Sigma.ι A i)).hom)
    have hSum : Function.Bijective sumComparison := hSmall I A
    let freeSum : (I →₀ R) ≃ₗ[R] DirectSum I (fun _ => ↥(H.obj P)) :=
      (finsuppLEquivDirectSum R R I).trans (DirectSum.congrLinearEquiv fun _ => regular)
    exact ⟨(freeSum.trans (LinearEquiv.ofBijective sumComparison hSum)).toModuleIso⟩

  -- Alphabeta Math, step 2.1. Theorem 5.8 supplies the free terms and
  -- the cokernel universal property. The ring, module carriers, both
  -- index types, and the factorization targets are in universe v.
  -- The earlier checked ClassicalReconstruction result
  -- requires a supplied L with an adjunction and a unit formula.
  have hImage (V : ModuleCat.{v} R) : ∃ X : C, Nonempty (H.obj X ≅ V) := by
    have hPresent := FreeModulesAndPresentations.{v, v, v, v, v} R V
    obtain ⟨I, J, d, q, hRange, hSurj⟩ := hPresent.2.1
    obtain ⟨hZero, hFactor⟩ := (hPresent.2.2 d q).mp ⟨hRange, hSurj⟩
    let d' : ModuleCat.of R (J →₀ R) ⟶ ModuleCat.of R (I →₀ R) := ModuleCat.ofHom d
    let q' : ModuleCat.of R (I →₀ R) ⟶ V := ModuleCat.ofHom q
    have hdq : CategoryStruct.comp d' q' = 0 := ModuleCat.hom_ext hZero
    let _ : Epi q' := (ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective q').2 hSurj
    have hV : IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ q' hdq) := by
      refine CokernelCofork.IsColimit.ofπ' q' hdq (fun {N} g hg => ?_)
      have hZeroG : g.hom.comp d = 0 := congrArg ModuleCat.Hom.hom hg
      let factor := Classical.indefiniteDescription _ (hFactor N g.hom hZeroG).exists
      exact ⟨ModuleCat.ofHom factor.1, ModuleCat.hom_ext factor.2⟩

    -- Lift the relation map conjugated by the free comparisons. The
    -- two resulting coforks are colimiting by Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 5.8.
    obtain ⟨thetaI⟩ := hFree I
    obtain ⟨thetaJ⟩ := hFree J
    let lifted := H.preimage (CategoryStruct.comp thetaJ.inv (CategoryStruct.comp d' thetaI.hom))
    have hSquare : CategoryStruct.comp thetaJ.hom (H.map lifted) =
        CategoryStruct.comp d' thetaI.hom := by
      simp [lifted]
    let _ : PreservesColimit (parallelPair lifted 0) H := hExact.2.1 lifted
    have hMapped := isColimitOfHasCokernelOfPreservesColimit H lifted
    exact ⟨cokernel lifted, ⟨(CokernelCofork.mapIsoOfIsColimit hV hMapped
      (Arrow.isoMk' d' (H.map lifted) thetaJ thetaI hSquare)).symm⟩⟩

  -- Alphabeta Math, steps 3.1 and 4.1 conclude via the given
  -- adjunction. Theorem 8.6 asks for a quasi-inverse and both natural
  -- isomorphisms. Mathlib chooses the preimages above and defines the
  -- inverse on maps by conjugation and fullness. Faithfulness gives
  -- the functor laws and naturality of the comparison lifted to C.
  -- This packages the notes’ pointwise cokernel construction with
  -- classical choice of preimages under §8.1. The reviewed endpoint
  -- only requires the resulting functor and natural isomorphisms.
  let _ : H.EssSurj := ⟨hImage⟩
  let _ : H.IsEquivalence := { }
  let e := H.asEquivalence
  exact ⟨e.inverse, ⟨e.counitIso⟩, ⟨e.unitIso.symm⟩⟩)

TensorPreservesCoproducts.proof:
by
  intro R _ S _ Bimod star B carrier right Balanced T pure hT I M
  -- This is the lecture notes' ordinary-choice endpoint. The reviewed
  -- inclusions use Classical.decEq and the family of lifts is selected below.
  let _ : DecidableEq I := Classical.decEq I
  let X (j : I) : Type _ := M j
  let Y (j : I) : Type _ := T (M j)
  let A := ModuleCat.of R (DirectSum I X)
  let D := ModuleCat.of S (DirectSum I Y)
  let inX (j : I) := DirectSum.lof R I X j
  let inY (j : I) := DirectSum.lof S I Y j
  change ∃ e : D ≃ₗ[S] T A, ∀ j x y, e (inY j (pure (M j) x y)) = pure A x (inX j y)
  -- BimoduleTensorFunctoriality supplies one model of the tensor functor.
  -- The checked concrete_tensor_direct_sum_iso uses common ring and carrier
  -- universes and concrete tensor and sum models. The endpoint has arbitrary
  -- T and independent universes, so construct the maps from hT.
  -- Use uniqueness in hT for pure-tensor extensionality (Alphabeta Math F1 and F3).
  have pureExt (N : ModuleCat R) (E : AddCommGrpCat)
      (f g : T N →+ E) (agree : ∀ x y, f (pure N x y) = g (pure N x y)) : f = g := by
    have balanced : Balanced N E (fun x y => g (pure N x y)) := by
      obtain ⟨addLeft, addRight, balance⟩ := (hT N).1
      exact ⟨fun x x' y => (congrArg g (addLeft x x' y)).trans (map_add g _ _),
        fun x y y' => (congrArg g (addRight x y y')).trans (map_add g _ _),
        fun a x y => congrArg g (balance a x y)⟩
    obtain ⟨_, _, unique⟩ := (hT N).2.1 E (fun x y => g (pure N x y)) balanced
    exact (unique f agree).trans (unique g (fun _ _ => rfl)).symm
  -- Step 2.1. Compare the two additive maps obtained by putting a scalar on
  -- either side of the lift. The specified action on pure tensors proves equality.
  have liftLinear (N : ModuleCat R) (E : ModuleCat S) (p : carrier → N → E)
      (hp : Balanced N E p) (outer : ∀ (c : S) x y, p (c • x) y = c • p x y) :
      ∃ f : T N →ₗ[S] E, ∀ x y, f (pure N x y) = p x y := by
    obtain ⟨f, hf, _⟩ := (hT N).2.1 (AddCommGrpCat.of E) p hp
    refine ⟨{ f with map_smul' := ?_ }, hf⟩
    intro c z
    change f (c • z) = c • f z
    have commute : f.comp (DistribSMul.toAddMonoidHom (T N) c) =
        (DistribSMul.toAddMonoidHom E c).comp f := by
      apply pureExt N (AddCommGrpCat.of E)
      intro x y
      change f (c • pure N x y) = c • f (pure N x y)
      rw [(hT N).2.2, hf, hf, outer]
    exact DFunLike.congr_fun commute z
  -- Step 1.2. Lift each inclusion using the balancing and outer action of
  -- pure A, then assemble the lifts via the linear direct-sum universal
  -- property underlying ModuleProductsAndCoproducts.
  have existsLeg (j : I) :
      ∃ f : T (M j) →ₗ[S] T A, ∀ x y, f (pure (M j) x y) = pure A x (inX j y) := by
    apply liftLinear (M j) (T A)
    · obtain ⟨addLeft, addRight, balance⟩ := (hT A).1
      exact ⟨fun x x' y => addLeft x x' (inX j y),
        fun x y y' => (congrArg (pure A x) (map_add (inX j) y y')).trans (addRight x _ _),
        fun a x y => (balance a x (inX j y)).trans
          (congrArg (pure A x) ((inX j).map_smul a y).symm)⟩
    · intro c x y
      exact ((hT A).2.2 c x (inX j y)).symm
  choose leg legPure using existsLeg
  let forward : D →ₗ[S] T A := DirectSum.toModule S I (T A) leg
  have forwardPure (j : I) (x : carrier) (y : M j) :
      forward (inY j (pure (M j) x y)) = pure A x (inX j y) := by
    exact (DirectSum.toModule_lof S j _).trans (legPure j x y)
  -- Step 1.3. Assemble the coordinate pairing via the additive direct-sum
  -- universal property. This handles finite support internally, and gives the
  -- same inverse formula as the coordinatewise construction in the source.
  let pureRight (N : ModuleCat R) (x : carrier) : N →+ T N :=
    AddMonoidHom.mk' (pure N x) ((hT N).1.2.1 x)
  let pair (x : carrier) : A →+ D :=
    DirectSum.toAddMonoid (fun j => (inY j).toAddMonoidHom.comp (pureRight (M j) x))
  have pairIn (x : carrier) (j : I) (y : M j) :
      pair x (inX j y) = inY j (pure (M j) x y) :=
    DirectSum.toAddMonoid_of
      (fun k => (inY k).toAddMonoidHom.comp (pureRight (M k) x)) j y
  have sumExt (E : AddCommGrpCat) (f g : A →+ E)
      (agree : ∀ j y, f (inX j y) = g (inX j y)) : f = g :=
    DirectSum.addHom_ext agree
  have pairAdd (x x' : carrier) : pair (x + x') = pair x + pair x' := by
    apply sumExt (AddCommGrpCat.of D)
    intro j y
    change pair (x + x') (inX j y) = pair x (inX j y) + pair x' (inX j y)
    rw [pairIn, pairIn, pairIn, (hT (M j)).1.1, map_add]
  have pairBalance (a : R) (x : carrier) :
      pair (right a x) = (pair x).comp (DistribSMul.toAddMonoidHom A a) := by
    apply sumExt (AddCommGrpCat.of D)
    intro j y
    change pair (right a x) (inX j y) = pair x (a • inX j y)
    rw [← map_smul (inX j), pairIn, pairIn, (hT (M j)).1.2.2]
  have pairOuter (c : S) (x : carrier) :
      pair (c • x) = (DistribSMul.toAddMonoidHom D c).comp (pair x) := by
    apply sumExt (AddCommGrpCat.of D)
    intro j y
    change pair (c • x) (inX j y) = c • pair x (inX j y)
    rw [pairIn, pairIn, ← (hT (M j)).2.2]
    exact (inY j).map_smul c _
  obtain ⟨backward, backwardPure⟩ := liftLinear A D (fun x y => pair x y)
    ⟨fun x x' y => DFunLike.congr_fun (pairAdd x x') y,
      fun x y y' => map_add (pair x) y y',
      fun a x y => DFunLike.congr_fun (pairBalance a x) y⟩
    (fun c x y => DFunLike.congr_fun (pairOuter c x) y)
  -- Step 2.2. Compare the composites with the identities on the two kinds
  -- of generators. The universal properties apply to the empty family too.
  have forwardBackward : forward.comp backward = LinearMap.id := by
    apply LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_injective
    apply pureExt A (AddCommGrpCat.of (T A))
    intro x y
    change forward (backward (pure A x y)) = pure A x y
    rw [backwardPure]
    have agree : forward.toAddMonoidHom.comp (pair x) = pureRight A x := by
      apply sumExt (AddCommGrpCat.of (T A))
      intro j z
      change forward (pair x (inX j z)) = pure A x (inX j z)
      rw [pairIn, forwardPure]
    exact DFunLike.congr_fun agree y
  have backwardForward : backward.comp forward = LinearMap.id := by
    apply DirectSum.linearMap_ext
    intro j
    apply LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_injective
    apply pureExt (M j) (AddCommGrpCat.of D)
    intro x y
    change backward (forward (inY j (pure (M j) x y))) = inY j (pure (M j) x y)
    rw [forwardPure, backwardPure, pairIn]
  exact ⟨LinearEquiv.ofLinearMap forward backward forwardBackward backwardForward, forwardPure⟩

external.usage: DirectSum.toModule assembles the S-linear tensor maps of the summand inclusions. DirectSum.toModule_lof computes the comparison on the included tensors, and DirectSum.linearMap_ext reduces the inverse-after-forward identity to its restrictions to the summands. Independent index, summand and codomain universes and local decidable equality apply to the reviewed direct sums.

Assembles the inverse pairing as an additive map on the input direct sum for each fixed bimodule element. Its formula and additive extensionality on summand inclusions prove balance, additivity in the bimodule variable, outer linearity, and the forward-after-inverse identity. The additive and linear inclusions agree definitionally. All results apply to an arbitrary index type with the reviewed decidable equality, including the empty family.

CanonicalWattsNaturalTransformation.proof:
by
  intro R S _ _ F _ A B down right lambda Balanced T pure hT hMap
  -- Ian X, Lemma 9.3 (p. 29), env-9-3 in the cached TeX and PDF.
  -- https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf#page=29
  -- Alphabeta Math, steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-canonical-eilenberg-watts-comparison-is-balanced-and-natural
  -- The reviewed endpoint supplies T, its pure tensors, and their universal,
  -- scalar and morphism formulas. The checked CanonicalWattsComparison builds
  -- a comparison for a specific Finsupp quotient. Here the supplied universal
  -- property constructs the components for the given T.
  -- The pairing and composition lemmas below come from NotesProofs/WattsSupport.lean,
  -- source SHA-256 853d1dd0016bf0735f7a84559e2f1cbbb701fc3cb0e00395a0e138ffecb1f967
  -- (beta_balanced at line 237 and ell_comp at line 231).
  let G := F.comp (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{max u z, w} S)
  let beta : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R, B → M → G.obj M :=
    fun M b m => ULift.up ((F.map (lambda M m)).hom b)
  -- Step 1.1. The supplier uses the same lifted regular module, conjugated
  -- right multiplication and evaluation map. Carry its balance through ULift.
  have beta_balanced (M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R) : Balanced M (AddCommGrpCat.of (G.obj M)) (beta M) := by
    have h := ChoiceFreeWatts.beta_balanced F M
    exact ⟨fun b b' m => congrArg ULift.up (h.1 b b' m),
      fun b m m' => congrArg ULift.up (h.2.1 b m m'),
      fun r b m => congrArg ULift.up (h.2.2 r b m)⟩
  have beta_smul (M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R) (s : S) (b : B) (m : M) :
      beta M (s • b) m = s • beta M b m :=
    congrArg ULift.up ((F.map (lambda M m)).hom.map_smul s b)
  -- Step 2.1. Derive the pure-tensor equality test from the supplied
  -- uniqueness clause, which also works for the two naturality composites.
  have pure_ext (M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R) (Y : AddCommGrpCat.{max u z w}) (f g : T.obj M →+ Y)
      (h : ∀ b m, f (pure M b m) = g (pure M b m)) : f = g := by
    let p : B → M → Y := fun b m => g (pure M b m)
    have hb := (hT M).1
    have hp : Balanced M Y p := by
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro b b' m
        change g (pure M (b + b') m) = g (pure M b m) + g (pure M b' m)
        rw [hb.1, map_add]
      · intro b m m'
        change g (pure M b (m + m')) = g (pure M b m) + g (pure M b m')
        rw [hb.2.1, map_add]
      · intro r b m
        exact congrArg (fun x => g x) (hb.2.2 r b m)
    obtain ⟨k, _, hk⟩ := (hT M).2.1 Y p hp
    exact (hk f h).trans (hk g (fun _ _ => rfl)).symm
  have exists_lift (M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R) :
      ∃ h : T.obj M →+ G.obj M, ∀ b m, h (pure M b m) = beta M b m := by
    obtain ⟨h, hh, _⟩ :=
      (hT M).2.1 (AddCommGrpCat.of (G.obj M)) (beta M) (beta_balanced M)
    exact ⟨h, hh⟩
  -- Use the unique additive lifts in the article's ordinary-choice setting.
  let lift (M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R) : T.obj M →+ G.obj M := Classical.choose (exists_lift M)
  have lift_pure (M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R) (b : B) (m : M) : lift M (pure M b m) = beta M b m :=
    Classical.choose_spec (exists_lift M) b m
  let appLin (M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R) : T.obj M →ₗ[S] G.obj M :=
    { lift M with
      map_smul' := by
        intro s x
        change lift M (s • x) = s • lift M x
        let actT : T.obj M →+ T.obj M := DistribSMul.toAddMonoidHom (T.obj M) s
        let actG : G.obj M →+ G.obj M := DistribSMul.toAddMonoidHom (G.obj M) s
        have hs : (lift M).comp actT = actG.comp (lift M) := by
          apply pure_ext M (AddCommGrpCat.of (G.obj M))
          intro b m
          change lift M (s • pure M b m) = s • lift M (pure M b m)
          rw [(hT M).2.2, lift_pure, lift_pure, beta_smul]
        exact DFunLike.congr_fun hs x }
  have app_pure (M : ModuleCat.{max u z} R) (b : B) (m : M) : appLin M (pure M b m) = beta M b m :=
    lift_pure M b m
  let τ : CategoryTheory.NatTrans T G :=
    { app := fun M => ModuleCat.ofHom (appLin M)
      naturality := by
        intro M N f
        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
        apply LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_injective
        apply pure_ext M (AddCommGrpCat.of (G.obj N))
        intro b m
        -- Step 3.1. Evaluate the supplied tensor map on generators and
        -- use the regular-module identity for the composite with f.
        change appLin N ((T.map f).hom (pure M b m)) =
          (G.map f).hom (appLin M (pure M b m))
        rw [hMap, app_pure, app_pure]
        change ULift.up ((F.map (lambda N (f.hom m))).hom b) =
          ULift.up ((F.map f).hom ((F.map (lambda M m)).hom b))
        congr 1
        calc
          _ = _ := congrArg (fun k => (F.map k).hom b) (ChoiceFreeWatts.ell_comp f m).symm
          _ = _ := congrArg (fun k => k.hom b) (F.map_comp (lambda M m) f) }
  exact ⟨τ, app_pure⟩

RegularModuleTensorUnits.proof:
by
  intro R _ regularRight LeftTensor leftPure RightMod right RightTensor rightPure
  let leftAdd (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) : AddCommGroup (LeftTensor M) :=
    ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorAddCommGroup (X := M) regularRight
  let leftModule (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) : Module R (LeftTensor M) :=
    ChoiceFreeWatts.outerModule (X := M) regularRight (fun (r a x : R) => mul_assoc a x r)
  let rightAdd (B : RightMod) : AddCommGroup (RightTensor B) :=
    ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorAddCommGroup (X := R) (right B)
  -- Ian X, Theorem 6.4, p. 19.
  -- https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf#page=19
  -- Alphabeta Math, steps 1.1–4.1.
  -- https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products
  -- BimoduleTensorFunctoriality supplies a categorical existence theorem with
  -- lifted carriers. Here the endpoint fixes the unlifted quotient and independent
  -- universes. Use its underlying WattsSupport lifts and pure-tensor extensionality
  -- directly on that quotient. The checked NotesProofs/WattsSupport.lean
  -- (SHA-256 853d1dd0016bf0735f7a84559e2f1cbbb701fc3cb0e00395a0e138ffecb1f967)
  -- supplies pureBalanced, tensorLift, tensorLift_pure, tensorLinearLift,
  -- tensorLinearLift_pure, tensorExt, tensorAddCommGroup, and outerModule.
  -- The common-universe ConcreteTensorUnitor uses ULift on the regular factor.
  -- The balance calculations below use literal R in that factor.
  -- Mathlib's TensorProduct.lid and TensorProduct.rid assume a commutative
  -- base semiring. The endpoint permits arbitrary unital rings.
  constructor
  · -- Steps 1.1 and 3.1: balance uses mul_smul, which also gives outer linearity.
    have comm (r a x : R) : regularRight r (a • x) = a • regularRight r x :=
      mul_assoc a x r
    have balanced (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) :
        ChoiceFreeWatts.Balanced regularRight (fun (r : R) (m : M) => r • m) :=
      ⟨fun r s m => add_smul r s m, fun r m n => smul_add r m n,
        fun a r m => mul_smul r a m⟩
    let eval (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) : LeftTensor M →ₗ[R] M :=
      ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLinearLift regularRight comm (fun r m => r • m)
        (balanced M) (fun a r m => mul_smul a r m)
    have eval_pure (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) (r : R) (m : M) :
        eval M (leftPure M r m) = r • m :=
      ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLinearLift_pure regularRight comm _ (balanced M) _ r m
    -- Step 2.1: insertion of one is additive and its composite with evaluation
    -- is tested on the pure generators by tensorExt.
    let insert (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) : M →+ LeftTensor M :=
      AddMonoidHom.mk' (leftPure M 1) ((ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced regularRight).2.1 1)
    have insert_eval (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) (z : LeftTensor M) :
        insert M (eval M z) = z := by
      have h : (insert M).comp (eval M).toAddMonoidHom = AddMonoidHom.id _ := by
        apply ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorExt regularRight
        intro r m
        change leftPure M 1 (eval M (leftPure M r m)) = leftPure M r m
        rw [eval_pure]
        simpa only [regularRight, one_mul] using
          ((ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced (X := M) regularRight).2.2 r 1 m).symm
      exact DFunLike.congr_fun h z
    let unit (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) : LeftTensor M ≃ₗ[R] M :=
      { eval M with
        invFun := insert M
        left_inv := insert_eval M
        right_inv := fun m => (eval_pure M 1 m).trans (one_smul R m) }
    refine ⟨unit, eval_pure, ?_⟩
    -- The article's naturality square is witnessed by conjugating each module
    -- morphism by the unit. Its pure formula follows from linearity and evaluation.
    intro M N f
    let tf := (unit N).symm.toLinearMap.comp (f.hom.comp (unit M).toLinearMap)
    refine ⟨tf, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro r m
      apply (unit N).injective
      change unit N ((unit N).symm (f (unit M (leftPure M r m)))) =
        unit N (leftPure N r (f m))
      rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
      change f (eval M (leftPure M r m)) = eval N (leftPure N r (f m))
      rw [eval_pure, eval_pure]
      exact f.hom.map_smul r m
    · intro z
      exact (unit N).apply_symm_apply (f (unit M z))
  · -- Step 1.2: op a acts as right multiplication by a. Hence evaluation
    -- on ((b a), r) uses op r * op a = op (a * r).
    have balanced (B : RightMod) : ChoiceFreeWatts.Balanced (right B)
        (fun (b : B) (r : R) => right B r b) := by
      refine ⟨fun b c r => smul_add (MulOpposite.op r) b c, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro b r t
        exact add_smul (MulOpposite.op r) (MulOpposite.op t) b
      · intro a b r
        exact (mul_smul (MulOpposite.op r) (MulOpposite.op a) b).symm
    let eval (B : RightMod) : RightTensor B →+ B :=
      ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLift (right B) (fun b r => right B r b) (balanced B)
    have eval_pure (B : RightMod) (b : B) (r : R) :
        eval B (rightPure B b r) = right B r b :=
      ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLift_pure (right B) _ (balanced B) b r
    -- Step 1.2 also gives the inverse: insert one, then use balance at one
    -- to check the tensor-side composite on the generators.
    let insert (B : RightMod) : B →+ RightTensor B :=
      AddMonoidHom.mk' (fun b => rightPure B b 1)
        (fun b c => (ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced (X := R) (right B)).1 b c 1)
    have insert_eval (B : RightMod) (z : RightTensor B) :
        insert B (eval B z) = z := by
      have h : (insert B).comp (eval B) = AddMonoidHom.id _ := by
        apply ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorExt (right B)
        intro b r
        change rightPure B (eval B (rightPure B b r)) 1 = rightPure B b r
        rw [eval_pure]
        simpa only [smul_eq_mul, mul_one] using
          (ChoiceFreeWatts.pureBalanced (X := R) (right B)).2.2 r b (1 : R)
      exact DFunLike.congr_fun h z
    let equiv (B : RightMod) : RightTensor B ≃+ B :=
      { eval B with
        invFun := insert B
        left_inv := insert_eval B
        right_inv := fun b => (eval_pure B b 1).trans (one_smul (MulOpposite R) b) }
    -- Step 3.1: transfer the right action across the additive isomorphism.
    -- Its pure formula identifies it with right multiplication on the second
    -- factor. This implements the action on the particular reviewed quotient.
    let rightModule (B : RightMod) : Module (MulOpposite R) (RightTensor B) :=
      (equiv B).module (MulOpposite R)
    let unit (B : RightMod) : RightTensor B ≃ₗ[MulOpposite R] B :=
      (equiv B).linearEquiv (MulOpposite R)
    refine ⟨rightModule, unit, eval_pure, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro B a r b
      apply (unit B).injective
      rw [(unit B).map_smul]
      change MulOpposite.op a • eval B (rightPure B b r) =
        eval B (rightPure B b (r * a))
      rw [eval_pure, eval_pure]
      exact (mul_smul (MulOpposite.op a) (MulOpposite.op r) b).symm
    · -- As on the left, conjugation proves the naturality square at every tensor.
      intro B C g
      let tg := (unit C).symm.toLinearMap.comp (g.hom.comp (unit B).toLinearMap)
      refine ⟨tg, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro b r
        apply (unit C).injective
        change unit C ((unit C).symm (g (unit B (rightPure B b r)))) =
          unit C (rightPure C (g b) r)
        rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
        change g (eval B (rightPure B b r)) = eval C (rightPure C (g b) r)
        rw [eval_pure, eval_pure]
        exact g.hom.map_smul (MulOpposite.op r) b
      · intro z
        exact (unit C).apply_symm_apply (g (unit B z))
    · -- Steps 3.1 and 4.1: the bimodule hypothesis makes the pairing S-linear.
      -- Compare its S-linear lift with evaluation on generators. Injectivity of
      -- the right unit then carries commutation of the two actions back to tensors.
      intro S _ B _ _
      let commute (r : R) (a : S) (b : B) :
          right B r (a • b) = a • right B r b :=
        smul_comm (MulOpposite.op r) a b
      let : Module S (RightTensor B) :=
        ChoiceFreeWatts.outerModule (X := R) (right B) commute
      let outerEval : RightTensor B →ₗ[S] B :=
        ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLinearLift (right B) commute
          (fun b r => right B r b) (balanced B) (fun a b r => commute r a b)
      have eval_eq : outerEval.toAddMonoidHom = eval B :=
        ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorExt (right B) _ _ (fun b r =>
          (ChoiceFreeWatts.tensorLinearLift_pure (right B) commute _
            (balanced B) (fun a b r => commute r a b) b r).trans (eval_pure B b r).symm)
      have outer_smul (a : S) (z : RightTensor B) : unit B (a • z) = a • unit B z := by
        change eval B (a • z) = a • eval B z
        rw [← eval_eq]
        exact outerEval.map_smul a z
      refine ⟨⟨?_⟩, outer_smul⟩
      intro a c z
      apply (unit B).injective
      rw [(unit B).map_smul, outer_smul, outer_smul, (unit B).map_smul]

TensorPreservesCokernels.proof:
by
  classical
  intro R _ S _ Bimod star B carrier right Balanced T _ pure properties mapPure
  -- Alphabeta Math, steps 1.4–1.5. Uniqueness in the balanced universal
  -- property gives pure-tensor extensionality for the abstract T. Proposition
  -- 6.3 (BimoduleTensorFunctoriality) supplies the construction of a bifunctor.
  -- Its fixed-bimodule laws are hypotheses of this theorem.
  -- NotesProofs.balanced_tensor_preserves_cokernel groups both rings in one
  -- universe and all carriers in another, and assumes S-linear lifts.
  -- The descent here uses the reviewed T and leaves the universes independent.
  have addExt (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) (D : AddCommGrpCat.{max v w t})
      (f g : AddMonoidHom (T.obj M) D)
      (h : ∀ b m, f (pure M b m) = g (pure M b m)) : f = g := by
    let pairing : carrier → M → D := fun b m => g (pure M b m)
    have hb : Balanced M D pairing := by
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro b b' m
        dsimp [pairing]
        rw [(properties M).1.1, map_add]
      · intro b m m'
        dsimp [pairing]
        rw [(properties M).1.2.1, map_add]
      · intro a b m
        dsimp [pairing]
        rw [(properties M).1.2.2]
    obtain ⟨k, _, unique⟩ := (properties M).2.1 D pairing hb
    exact (unique f h).trans (unique g (fun _ _ => rfl)).symm
  have homExt (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) (D : ModuleCat.{max v w t} S)
      (f g : T.obj M ⟶ D)
      (h : ∀ b m, f (pure M b m) = g (pure M b m)) : f = g := by
    have eq := addExt M (AddCommGrpCat.of D) f.hom.toAddMonoidHom g.hom.toAddMonoidHom h
    exact ModuleCat.hom_ext (LinearMap.ext fun x => DFunLike.congr_fun eq x)
  -- Step 2.1: the outer action formula holds for pure tensors by hypothesis.
  -- Compare two additive maps for each scalar to get linearity on every tensor.
  have lift (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) (D : ModuleCat.{max v w t} S)
      (p : carrier → M → D) (hp : Balanced M D p)
      (outer : ∀ (a : S) b m, p (a • b) m = a • p b m) :
      ∃ k : T.obj M ⟶ D, ∀ b m, k (pure M b m) = p b m := by
    obtain ⟨k, hk, _⟩ := (properties M).2.1 (AddCommGrpCat.of D) p hp
    have linear (a : S) (x : T.obj M) : k (a • x) = a • k x := by
      let scale (A : ModuleCat.{max v w t} S) : A →+ A :=
        { toFun := fun y => a • y
          map_zero' := smul_zero a
          map_add' := smul_add a }
      have he := addExt M (AddCommGrpCat.of D) (k.comp (scale (T.obj M)))
        ((scale D).comp k) (by
          intro b m
          change k (a • pure M b m) = a • k (pure M b m)
          rw [(properties M).2.2, hk, hk, outer])
      exact DFunLike.congr_fun he x
    let kLinear : T.obj M →ₗ[S] D :=
      { k with
        map_smul' := linear }
    exact ⟨ModuleCat.ofHom kLinear, hk⟩
  have preserve (C : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{w} R))
      (exactC : C.Exact) (epiC : Epi C.g) :
      Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ (C.map T).g (C.map T).zero)) := by
    -- Steps 1.4–1.5, F6 and F7: obtain actual lifts, including lifts of the
    -- differences of two representatives, from the two exactness hypotheses.
    have surj : Function.Surjective C.g :=
      (ModuleKernelsCokernelsAndImages R C.g).2.2.2.2.2.2.mp epiC
    have preimage (n : C.X₂) (hn : C.g n = 0) : ∃ m : C.X₁, C.f m = n := by
      have hrange : LinearMap.range C.f.hom = LinearMap.ker C.g.hom :=
        (ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff_range_eq_ker C).mp exactC
      have hker := ((ModuleKernelsCokernelsAndImages R C.g).1 n).mpr hn
      exact ((ModuleKernelsCokernelsAndImages R C.f).2.1 n).mp (hrange.symm ▸ hker)
    -- Step 1.4: ShortComplex.map gives the zero composite because T is
    -- additive. Step 1.5 applies the notes' representative argument to each
    -- S-linear test map to obtain the universal property directly
    -- (Theorem 6.7, pp. 20–21).
    have factor (D : ModuleCat.{max v w t} S) (h : T.obj C.X₂ ⟶ D)
        (hh : T.map C.f ≫ h = 0) :
        ∃ k : T.obj C.X₃ ⟶ D, T.map C.g ≫ k = h := by
      have independent (b : carrier) (n n' : C.X₂) (eq : C.g n = C.g n') :
          h (pure C.X₂ b n) = h (pure C.X₂ b n') := by
        obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := preimage (n - n') (by rw [map_sub, eq, sub_self])
        have vanish : h (pure C.X₂ b (n - n')) = 0 := by
          rw [← hm, ← mapPure C.f]
          exact ConcreteCategory.congr_hom hh (pure C.X₁ b m)
        calc
          h (pure C.X₂ b n) = h (pure C.X₂ b (n - n' + n')) := by rw [sub_add_cancel]
          _ = h (pure C.X₂ b n') := by
            rw [(properties C.X₂).1.2.1, map_add, vanish, zero_add]
      -- The notes permit ordinary choice. Both this representative and the
      -- colimit desc below use Classical.choice. The portal's steps 1.5
      -- and 3.1 rely on independence of the representative to obtain a
      -- uniquely defined value. The present article formalization chooses a
      -- representative from the given surjection and proves that independence.
      let p : carrier → C.X₃ → D := fun b x => h (pure C.X₂ b (surj x).choose)
      have p_apply (b : carrier) (n : C.X₂) : p b (C.g n) = h (pure C.X₂ b n) :=
        independent b _ _ (surj (C.g n)).choose_spec
      have bp : Balanced C.X₃ D p := by
        refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro b b' x
          obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := surj x
          simp only [p_apply, (properties C.X₂).1.1, map_add]
        · intro b x x'
          obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := surj x
          obtain ⟨n', rfl⟩ := surj x'
          have qadd : C.g (n + n') = C.g n + C.g n' := C.g.hom.map_add n n'
          rw [← qadd, p_apply, p_apply, p_apply, (properties C.X₂).1.2.1, map_add]
        · intro a b x
          obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := surj x
          have qsmul : C.g (a • n) = a • C.g n := map_smul C.g.hom a n
          rw [← qsmul, p_apply, p_apply, (properties C.X₂).1.2.2]
      have outer (a : S) (b : carrier) (x : C.X₃) : p (a • b) x = a • p b x := by
        obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := surj x
        rw [p_apply, p_apply, ← (properties C.X₂).2.2, map_smul]
      obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := lift C.X₃ D p bp outer
      refine ⟨k, homExt C.X₂ D _ _ ?_⟩
      intro b n
      change k ((T.map C.g) (pure C.X₂ b n)) = h (pure C.X₂ b n)
      rw [mapPure C.g, hk, p_apply]
    refine ⟨CokernelCofork.IsColimit.ofπ (T.map C.g) (C.map T).zero
      (fun {_} h hh => (factor _ h hh).choose)
      (fun {_} h hh => (factor _ h hh).choose_spec) ?_⟩
    intro D h hh k hk
    apply homExt C.X₃ D
    intro b x
    obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := surj x
    rw [← mapPure C.g]
    exact (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom hk (pure C.X₂ b n)).trans
      (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (factor D h hh).choose_spec (pure C.X₂ b n)).symm
  -- Steps 1.4 and 3.1: the target cokernel gives both the kernel-image equality
  -- and epimorphy by Proposition 4.9 (ExactPresentationsAreCokernels). The
  -- same equivalence handles any input cokernel cofork. The zero-composite
  -- witnesses agree by proof irrelevance.
  -- Use the canonical ModuleCat abelian instance underlying
  -- ModuleCategoriesAreAbelian, so the existing zero-morphism instances match.
  constructor
  · intro C hexact hepi
    obtain ⟨_, h⟩ := (ExactPresentationsAreCokernels (T.map C.f) (T.map C.g)).mpr
      ⟨(C.map T).zero, preserve C hexact hepi⟩
    exact h
  · intro C hcokernel
    obtain ⟨_, hexact, hepi⟩ := (ExactPresentationsAreCokernels C.f C.g).mpr
      ⟨C.zero, hcokernel⟩
    exact preserve C hexact hepi

GroupAlgebraInductionAdjunction.proof:
by
  intro k _ G _ H
  dsimp only
  let R := MonoidAlgebra k (↥H)
  let S := MonoidAlgebra k G
  let i : R →+* S := MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainRingHom k H.subtype
  have hsub : Function.Injective (H.subtype : ↥H → G) := Subtype.val_injective
  have hsingle (h : ↥H) (a : k) :
      i (MonoidAlgebra.single h a) = MonoidAlgebra.single (h : G) a :=
    MonoidAlgebra.mapDomain_single
  -- Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 7.6, p. 24.
  -- https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf#page=24
  -- The subgroup inclusion has singleton fibers
  -- on the image and empty off it. Associativity gives commuting actions.
  refine ⟨MonoidAlgebra.mapDomain_injective hsub, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro a h
    exact Finsupp.mapDomain_apply_of_injective hsub (MonoidAlgebra.coeff a) h
  · intro a g hg
    exact Finsupp.mapDomain_of_notMem_range (MonoidAlgebra.coeff a) g
      (fun ⟨h, hh⟩ => hg (hh ▸ h.property))
  · intro a x
    rfl
  · let rightModule : Module (MulOpposite R) S := Module.compHom S (RingHom.op i)
    exact ⟨fun (a : MulOpposite R) (b x : S) =>
      (show (b * x) * i a.unop = b * (x * i a.unop) from mul_assoc _ _ _)⟩
  · intro W a z
    -- Theorem 7.4’s canonical conversion restricts along a ↦ a[1].
    -- The reviewed RepresentationModuleCorrespondence supplies existential
    -- witnesses. To identify the action of the endpoint’s specified functor,
    -- compute directly from Rep.ofModuleMonoidAlgebra.
    change i (MonoidAlgebra.single (1 : ↥H) a) • z =
      (MonoidAlgebra.single (1 : G) a : S) • z
    rw [hsingle]
    rfl
  · intro W h z
    change i (MonoidAlgebra.single h (1 : k)) • z =
      (MonoidAlgebra.single (h : G) (1 : k) : S) • z
    rw [hsingle]
  · obtain ⟨Ind, p, hp, hLift, hSmul, hMap⟩ :=
      GroupAlgebraInductionAux.tensorForRingMap.{max u v, max u v, w} i
    let pure (V : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) : S →+ (V →+ Ind.obj V) :=
      AddMonoidHom.mk' (fun x => AddMonoidHom.mk' (p V x) ((hp V).2.1 x))
        (fun x y => AddMonoidHom.ext ((hp V).1 x y))
    refine ⟨Ind, pure, ?_, hMap, GroupAlgebraInductionAux.tensorRestrictAdjunction i hp
      hLift hSmul hMap⟩
    intro V
    refine ⟨(hp V).2.2, ?_, hSmul V, ?_⟩
    · intro A _ q hq
      exact hLift V A (fun x z => q x z)
        ⟨fun x y z => by dsimp only; rw [map_add, AddMonoidHom.add_apply],
        fun x z z' => (q x).map_add z z', hq⟩
    · intro g x z
      exact hSmul V (MonoidAlgebra.single g (1 : k)) x z
